implementation_notes: The module is the well-known object: a module-scoped Map plus exported register/lookup functions, with ES module caching guaranteeing one registry instance per resolved specifier. What replaces the classic Registry class is that Map and module scope - no class or singleton accessor is needed. Two platform registries show the same idea narrower: Symbol.for/Symbol.keyFor maintain a runtime-wide global symbol registry keyed by string, and window.customElements (CustomElementRegistry) is the DOM's element registry, with scoped registries available through new CustomElementRegistry(). A factory that returns Map + functions is still justified when several independent registries must coexist (per test, per realm, per plugin host).
pitfalls: The registry is per module instance and per realm: a package loaded twice (dual CJS/ESM build, duplicated node_modules entry) yields two registries, so registrations made by one copy are invisible to the other.
A dev-server reload or HMR re-evaluates the module, replacing or duplicating registrations; keep long-lived registries out of hot-reloaded modules or hang them on globalThis under a symbol.
Map entries are strong references and are never collected; key by object and use WeakMap/WeakRef when entries should be collectable.
Symbol.for keys are runtime-wide, unremovable and not enumerable through the API, so they are a poor choice for a registry you need to list or reset.
